name: Ankit Chadha
tagline: Director of Applied Science at Amazon AGI. I lead science and engineering teams building grounded reasoning for AI agents, agent memory, and web-scale retrieval across text, images, and structured data.
meta_description: Ankit Chadha is a Director of Applied Science at Amazon AGI working on grounded reasoning for AI agents, agent memory, procedural knowledge graphs, retrieval-augmented generation, and multimodal web-scale search.
bio: I lead Applied Science and Engineering teams at Amazon AGI, turning research in foundation models and agents into systems that work at web scale. My work spans post-training and alignment, multimodal and grounded retrieval, agent memory, and evaluation. A recurring question connects it: how can an AI system find reliable evidence, reason over it, and retain useful experience? Previously I led deep learning work at Salesforce and worked at Apple and Samsung.
knows_about: post-training and alignment for large language models
preference optimization and reinforcement learning from feedback

themes.heading: Agent memory
themes.body: Introduced typed procedural knowledge graphs for reusable agent experience and append-only property graph memory for temporal conversational reasoning.

themes.heading: How agents delegate
themes.body: Introduced adaptive routing between typed dependency graphs and natural-language handoffs for multi-agent LLM systems.

themes.heading: Web-scale question answering
themes.body: Built web-scale document retrieval, passage reranking, and answer sentence selection methods spanning thirty million documents and nine languages.

themes.heading: Learning from data that cannot move
themes.body: Developed mixed-domain neural machine translation and communication-efficient federated learning without pooling data across domains.

themes.heading: Steering what a model says
themes.body: Developed methods for controlling toxicity, sentiment, simplicity, and viewpoint through hidden-state transformations and attribute conditioning.

education.degree: Graduate AI coursework, CS221, CS224n, CS231n, CS234

earlier_work_note: These are from my undergraduate years, in electronics and computer engineering rather than AI, and they appeared in low-selectivity, author-pays journals. I list them because they are genuinely mine and because they still account for a large share of my total citations, not because I would submit them anywhere today. Full text for all of them is on arXiv. Note that Aman Chadha, a co-author on two of these, is a different person.
